extracted.intended_audience: educators, curriculum planners, educational theorists, and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and applying standards for judging the worth, organization, and aims of school studies and curricula — focusing on intrinsic vs. instrumental value, motivation, integration, and the social consequences of curricular design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intrinsic (appreciation) value / appreciation
rubrics_metrics.description: Value as prizing or esteeming something for its own sake — a full or complete experience; appreciation is a direct, immediate good and not an object of comparative judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arts and studies should provide intensified, enhanced appreciation; they 'fix taste' and form standards for later experiences. Intrinsic value is characterized by direct enjoyment and cannot be ranked against other intrinsic goods. A subject ought in some aspect to be appreciable on its own account (e.g., arithmetic as well as poetry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrumental value / valuating
rubrics_metrics.description: Value as a means to some further end: to valuate or evaluate when choice among alternatives is required and one thing is judged in relation to another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instrumental values are judged by their contribution to some further end; they become meaningful only in relation to intrinsic goods that serve as the ultimate ends in particular situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate motivating value
rubrics_metrics.description: A topic that 'makes an immediate appeal' need not be justified by pointing to future utility; immediate responsiveness of pupils is itself proof of value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When pupils are genuinely concerned with a topic, that response is evidence it possesses value. Avoid forcing distant/utilitarian justifications for topics that are intrinsically engaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceptible instrumental connection
rubrics_metrics.description: When a topic is to be valued instrumentally, students should be enabled to perceive how it serves as a means to some intrinsic good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: enable students to discover that success in something they care about depends on numeric ability rather than lecturing about remote future benefits. Present material so the instrumental relation is evident to pupils.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use conscious consequences when intrinsic motive is absent
rubrics_metrics.description: If a pupil lacks natural appetite or has a perverted motive, conscious reference to results (consequences) is indicated to justify positive or negative value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers should make explicit the outcomes and connections when intrinsic interest does not motivate the pupil (e.g., health, appetite, corrective instruction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not establish a fixed hierarchy of studies
rubrics_metrics.description: It is futile to attempt to arrange studies in a single linear order from least to most valuable, because many studies have unique, irreplaceable functions and situational worth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid curricular schemes that rank subjects absolutely; valuation depends on situation and the specific contribution a study makes to living experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate subjects by realized outcomes, not assumed inherent values
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that a subject 'has' disciplinary, utilitarian, cultural, or moral value are justified only when the subject actually accomplishes those results in practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: blaming pupils when a subject 'fails' to produce its supposed values (assuming values inhered in the subject). Instead, assess teaching and conditions by evidence of achieved results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution to immediate intrinsic values is the primary test of worth
rubrics_metrics.description: The only criterion for determining the worth of instrumental and derived values in studies is their contribution to immediate intrinsic experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instrumental utilities are justified insofar as they increase the experienced content of life (i.e., help realize intrinsic goods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Present topics either as immediately valuable or clearly means-to-an-end
rubrics_metrics.description: Topics should be presented so that they either have immediate value requiring no justification or are perceived as means to attain intrinsic goods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid leaving topics in a limbo where neither intrinsic appeal nor clear instrumental connection is apparent to students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid segregation of educational values and promote unity of experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject the parceling out of separate, isolated values to segregated studies; aim for an integrated curriculum where interests reinforce one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate curricula by how well they prevent isolation (art vs science vs business) and instead foster overlap and mutual reinforcement among domains. In a democracy, education should struggle against social isolation of interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance breadth with efficiency; avoid overcrowding and narrow specialization
rubrics_metrics.description: Secure a broad and varied experience without sacrificing efficiency of execution; overcrowding the course of study leads to superficiality and harmful specialization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-patterns include: adding more studies to 'fix' gaps (creating a conglomerate curriculum), or reverting wholesale to a narrower traditional curriculum as a simplistic remedy. Prefer reorganization and integration over mere addition or quantitative cuts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use provisional classifications of values for survey and organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification (e.g., efficiency, sociability, aesthetic taste, trained intellectual method, conscientiousness) can be useful as provisional points of view for surveying and organizing instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such categories should not be treated as ultimate ends; they are heuristic devices to check proportion and distribution of experiences across the curriculum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constant inspection, criticism, and revision of curriculum
rubrics_metrics.description: Curricula require ongoing critical review to ensure they accomplish intended purposes and respond to present-day pupil needs rather than inherited adult values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for traditional matter or subjects that represent interests of adults or past generations rather than current pupils; revise to maintain relevance and motivating force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid treating subjects as containers of fixed 'values' (beware unconscious justification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Schemes that assign particular values to subjects often rationalize the existing curriculum rather than test it; values exist only insofar as the subject effects the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers and planners should not assume a subject 'trains' certain faculties by virtue of its name; inspect whether instruction produces the intended effects and revise methods accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer reorganizing content/methods over adding separate new studies
rubrics_metrics.description: New social or cultural interests should transform the aims and methods of existing instruction rather than be simply injected as additional subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: adding studies as patches which produce a time-table 'conglomerate' cemented by mechanics rather than coherence. Reorganization fosters integration and reduces overcrowding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide materials that furnish both direct enrichment and usable tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies included should furnish direct increments to pupils' lives and materials they can put to use in other concerns of direct interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curricular choices should be justified by both immediate enrichment and potential instrumental applicability in contexts meaningful to students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure democratic education combats social isolation of interests
rubrics_metrics.description: In democratic groups, education must work against social segregation so that various interests reinforce and play into one another, enriching common experience rather than dividing people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess curricula for their capacity to connect disparate interests (art, science, business, politics) and to promote shared experience and mutual understanding across social groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance preparation for useful labor and cultivation for leisure
rubrics_metrics.description: Education should contribute effectively to both gaining a livelihood (useful labor) and to living a cultivated, leisurely life; these aims should overlap rather than be opposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid hierarchical valuation that treats labor-training as inherently inferior. Curriculum design should seek overlap so education for leisure reinforces efficiency and vice versa.
